description: Before entering the Dungeon, Carl was a 27-year-old U.S. Coast Guard veteran who worked as a marine technician "fixing electrical systems for rich assholes and their party boats." He shared a two-bedroom apartment in Seattle, WA, with his girlfriend Beatrice and her award-winning cat, Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk.
notes: Crawler 4122. Coast Guard veteran, marine technician, Seattle.
Beatrice's award-winning show cat. Gains speech in the dungeon.

description: Beatrice's wealthy parents raised and showed Persian cats, and Beatrice proudly carried on the tradition: she took Donut to cat shows almost every weekend, and dedicated an entire bedroom of their two-bed apartment to displaying Donut's ribbons, trophies, and multitude of framed photos (plus a closet full of leggings).
notes: Carl's girlfriend and Donut's owner. Called Bea.

description: Sam has a reputation, at least by Donut's account, for being smelly and a bad influence: she recalls him coming over to play video games with Carl while the two "lied about their exploits with women," she still uses him as her benchmark for a bad smell, comparing an unwashed army camp on the Eleventh Floor to him. Carl remembers their friendship more fondly.
notes: Carl's friend on Earth.

description: Mordecai is the Royal Court's primary source of Dungeon lore, tactical advice, and high-level alchemy, and an indentured employee of Borant Corporation tasked with helping the corporation run crawls. Normally he works as a Game Guide for the first three floors and as a magic guild master on the later ones, where he has relative freedom to pursue potion making and catch up with friends.
notes: Non-combatant NPC. Guide and trainer to Carl and Donut.

description: Frank Q lived near Seattle and introduced himself to other crawlers as an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent. He is the talker of his partnership with Maggie My: calm, apologetic, reasonable, and a practiced enough liar to hold up under sustained questioning from Carl.

By Odette's account, Hekla was neither evil nor psychotic, but she was intensely practical and cunning, and she did not share Carl's sense of justice, which made her dangerous. Her voice carried very little emotion.

Chris is quiet but deeply empathetic, a capable maintenance and engineering hand with the same compulsive eye for looting that Carl has. His mother once mistook his silence for slowness and placed him in a special school, but as Brandon puts it, his brother is no fool, just a "Silent Bob" who is worth listening to on the rare occasions he speaks.

Before the Transformation, Imani was a caregiver at Meadow Lark Elder Care Facility in Wenatchee, WA. She entered the Dungeon with a number of patients and former staff members, and received a longsword in an early loot box.

An unneutered indoor-outdoor tomcat, Gravy Boat had fathered kittens on every female cat within three surrounding blocks and would sit in the tree outside the window whenever Donut was in heat. Beatrice called animal control on him twice without success and once got into a screaming fight with his owner over him.

Before her transformation in the Dungeon, Elle, pronounced "el," was a dotty, wheelchair-bound widow and full-time resident of the Meadow Lark Adult Care Community in Wenatchee, Washington. Her dementia left her only inconsistently aware of her surroundings, but she remained friendly, affectionate, and unexpectedly bawdy, startlingly blunt in her flirting with Carl.

Li Jun is a thoughtful, gentle man who cares deeply for his family and his friends, and he keeps a mostly positive attitude despite the horrors of the crawl. Offered points enough to pull one companion out of a hopeless fight and pressed to name that person, he refused to name anyone at all, telling Zhang they would die together instead.
Li Na was the only member of her starting party who did not work at the warehouse the other three came out of. Zhang, her brother's best friend, counts her as family anyway.

The Maestro (or Prince Maestro) is first introduced as host of Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, a production owned by his brother Prince Stalwart and funded by their father with what Zev describes as a small stipend.
notes: Show host and god sponsor.

description: Mongo is a highly aggressive and food-motivated dinosaur who views Princess Donut as his "mommy." Initially a hot-headed, untamable monster, he bonded with Donut after she taught him how to properly eviscerate Brindle Grubs. While he rarely listens to Carl, his loyalty to Donut is absolute, and he will instinctively throw himself into life-threatening danger to protect her.
notes: Donut's raptor companion.

description: Bringing fifteen goats into the Dungeon and keeping every one of them alive was unusual enough that Mordecai raised her with Carl as a curiosity.

Tsarina Signet is the protagonist of Vengeance of the Daughter, a scripted Syndicate drama built around her quest for revenge. The show presents her as a sympathetic outcast — the daughter of the High Elf King Finian and a Naiad princess — hunted by the High Elves as a mongrel child of the king and rejected by both sides of her heritage.
system_quote: The High-Elf King Finian, leader of the Liana Sector of the Hunting Grounds, was such a horny bastard, it was said he'd bedded women from over…
notes: Summoner and fairy-class NPC of the Over City.

description: Prepotente was one of fifteen brown-and-white Boer goats that Miriam Dom shepherded into the Dungeon. Fittingly, prepotente is Italian for arrogant, bossy, and overbearing. During Third Floor class selection he consumed an Enhanced Pet Biscuit and was transformed into a bipedal Caprid, emerging in a full set of armor with a double-headed battleaxe to fight at Miriam's side.
Florin fights with a magazine-fed Mossberg shotgun that never seems to run out of shells.

Katia was a university art professor in Reykjavík, Iceland, before the transformation. A single, well-traveled thirty-something, she's fluent in Icelandic, German, Russian, and English. She enters the Dungeon with her friend and fellow professor, Eva.

Quan Ch makes a poor first impression. Caught within the blast radius of a catastrophic failed spell, he publicly cursed out Carl and Donut in the group Quest chat rather than focusing on his own survival. His outburst earned him a swift block from Donut.

notes: The dungeon's administrative intelligence.
Surviving humans admitted to the dungeon.
Galactic authority that licenses the show.
Operator of this season of Dungeon Crawler World.
Species staffing safe rooms. Grouped as a faction; the schema has no species type.

description: Carl and Princess Donut were partied automatically the moment they descended into the Dungeon, since anyone entering at the same time is grouped by default. Donut holds Party Leader and dictates the group's branding and public-facing persona; Carl handles combat and supplies the explosives. Mongo, Donut's velociraptor pet, serves as Royal Steed.
notes: Donut's retinue of pets and followers.

description: Le Mouvement was a crawler party comprised of (150) African soldiers armed with AK-47s and at least one Red Cross worker. They were featured on the third episode of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth and descended to the Second Floor when the countdown timer struck 6 hours.

The Skull Empire is a Syndicate system government of orcs, separate from the Orcish Supremacy, the orcish system ruled by the Tusklings. Zev ranked it among the largest and oldest of the Syndicate's governments, and warned that it is not known for measured responses to insults. The empire spans multiple home systems, makes its money selling weapons, and was once described as a strong ally of the Valtay Corporation.

notes: Earth above the dungeon, before and during the Transformation.
Eighteen floors.

description: After the Transformation and subsequent System AI announcement, a trumpet-like horn sounds and 150,000 stairwells are randomly distributed in high population areas across Earth. Each stairwell entrance is marked by a spotlight-like light shining upward. Entering the stairwell is not enough to be classified as a "crawler." You must physically set foot on the First Floor.

The First Floor of the Dungeon is accessed from the surface-level staircases that populate the Earth after the Transformation, and is considered a tutorial floor. It is a sprawling grid of passages and tunnels that look like they were hewn out of rock, and is located below the Earth's surface.
notes: Tutorial level beneath the ruins.
Rest, storage, and a shop between encounters.

description: The Second Floor closely mirrors the maze-like layout of the First Floor, a giant grid of wide thoroughfares and twisting tunnels, though the main arteries here are narrower.
notes: Second tutorial level.
Third floor. Guarded medieval villages among monster-filled ruins, roughly the size of Arizona.
Members-only crawler club. Named on floor 1 by the Desperado Pass tattoo, though crawlers reach it later, so its reveal floor is 1.

description: Humans are a seeded race, sown by the Syndicate onto compatible worlds and left to grow unattended for thousands of years. Once a civilization takes hold — and as long as it has a working government — the Syndicate stages "First Contact," a legal milestone that clears it to return a couple thousand years later and strip the planet of its resources.
notes: Default race before third-floor selection.

description: The cat (Felis catus), or the house cat, is the only domesticated species in the family Felidae. Cats have strong flexible bodies, quick reflexes, retractable claws, sharp teeth, and well-developed night vision and sense of smell. Cats can hear sounds too faint or high-pitched for human ears, and both secrete and perceive pheromones.

Primals are known as the "boogiemen of the cosmos" and were the first known species to conquer the universe. After a great war spanning all corners of the galaxies, they vanished, leaving behind mysterious remnants of their civilization and technology, including Primal Engines.
system_quote: For the first several seasons of Dungeon Crawler World, all contestants started off as Primals…
notes: Carl's race, selected on the third floor.

description: Bopca are a stout, green-tinted, hairy dwarfish race that smell vaguely like wet moss. The females and males are equally shaggy. In general, Bopca are good cooks but known for having "a miserly streak"; giving discounts goes against their better nature.
notes: Safe-room attendant species.
Carl's class. Monk/rogue hybrid.
Donut's class. Bard/rogue jack-of-all-trades, Earth class.
Donut's merchant class, taken alongside Former Child Actor.
Katia Grim's class. Jouster, Earth class.
Monk class.
Earth class.
Hekla's class. Berserker.
Bautista's class. Swordsman.
Bard class.
Elle McGibbons's third-floor class.

description: Leveling up the skill allows crawlers to view more detailed information when inspecting explosives using the Heads-Up Display (HUD), and unlocks more crafting options. At Explosives Handling level 5, the crawler gains: * The crawler now receive additional information when inspecting explosive devices, such as Type, Status, and more details. See Goblin Smoke Bomb for an example.

IED is a skill gained and leveled by building improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Each level in the IED Skill increases the damage of improvised explosives by 10%, and decreases the chance of early detonation by 1/2.
system_quote: It’s one thing to take a grenade and toss it…

description: The Goblin Explosives Skill is a skill gained and leveled by handling gunpowder and goblin-made explosives such as Goblin Dynamite and Goblin Smoke Bombs. These devices are notoriously unstable.

Iron Punch is a monk/fighter skill that increases the amount of "enhanced fist" punching damage a crawler deals by 10% per skill level when the crawler wears a war gauntlet or lumper. It does not negate "bare knuckle" bonuses granted by the Pugilism Skill or Powerful Strike Skill. At level 10 it gains an upgrade called the Breadbasket Effect which provides a 10% chance to stun a mob for several seconds.
system_quote: When simple brutality isn’t enough. Newsboy cap not included…

description: At level 7, it can restore the crawler to full Health in approximately two minutes.
Light on Your Feet is a skill that allows a crawler to jump higher and farther with each skill level.
Category:Needs photo Foot Soldier is a melee skill that increases the damage a crawler does by kicking.

Determine Value is a skill that can most likely only be learned from a Skill Potion received in Loot Boxes. The first level of the skill allows a crawler to sort their inventory by item value, but the crawler cannot see the item's actual value or include items currently equipped.
system_quote: Hopefully now you’ll realize all those Magic: The Gathering cards are nothing more than just meaningless pieces of paper, and you should have spent your money…

description: The Chopper Pilot Skill is gained and leveled by driving a chopper, including Dungeon-made contraptions such as the Goblin Copper Chopper. Choppers are custom motorcycles "chopped" from existing motorcycles or built from scratch, which are marked by long front ends and frames without rear suspension. See Also: Goblin Copper Chopper#Operation for examples of leveling up
--> It most likely operates similar to the Explosives Handling Skill, in that higher levels of the skill allow crawlers to view more information about dangerous explosives.

notes: Grants Donut an extra class each floor.

description: Magic Missile is basic ranged attack spell that shoots hot laser bolts from the caster's eyes, one bolt after another. They look like laser blasts from a sci-fi movie, and can "be a little loud." The attack's power and operation change as it levels up. It can be modified by items such as the Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles.
notes: Spell.

description: Category:Needs photo Fire Fingers is a (presumably) low-cost spell that some crawlers learned on the First Floor. For thirty-one hours after the Dungeon opened, until the first patch update, the spell was not safe to cast.
notes: Spell.

description: The billowing cloud of fog is initially opaque but immediately becomes translucent to the caster, crawlers, and white-tagged NPCs; however, mobs remain blinded for its duration. While the fog is active, water beads on the ground and every surface. Scrolls of Confusing Fog are commonly received in Loot Boxes on the First Floor and Second Floor. Scrolls can be casted without spending mana points or learning the spell.
notes: Spell.

description: Puddle Jumper costs (20) mana to cast, and allows the caster and up to three other crawlers, NPCs, or pets to teleport to a surface within line of sight. The maximum allowable teleport distance increases with spell level, but the exact allowable distance is hidden. If the caster tries to teleport to a location that's too far way the spell will fail to cast.
notes: Spell.

description: The caster must have line of sight on their targets before they can begin casting. After spending (50) mana points, the caster is Rooted in Place for the full casting period (5 minutes at level one, 4 minutes at higher levels) and is surrounded by a shimmering golden glow that intensifies as the timer counts down. The glow is visible even if the caster is invisible.
notes: Spell.

description: If Fear is attempted to be cast on mobs that are scary themselves (such as Terror the Clown), the crawler will receive the following message: Warning: scary-ass mobs are immune to Fear effects. Entities under the Magical Fervor buff will be immune to Fear. An Alarm Module can be imbued with Fear, but for crawlers with a low Trap Engineer Skill, this can only be done at a Sapper's Table.
system_quote: Cost: 3 Mana If successfully cast, the effected mob either runs away, or stands its ground, but its Dexterity is lowered by an increasing amount per…
notes: Spell granted by Compensated Anarchist.

description: The Enchanted Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling is magical under-armor for melee fighters and tanks: it buffs health regeneration and makes the wearer immune to melee damage debuffs. This item can be upgraded. It is a form-fitting short-sleeve shirt that feels cool to the touch and is made of troll skin.
system_quote: The wearer of this shirt gains +7 to the Regeneration skill…
notes: Worn by Carl from the first hour.

description: The wearer of this cloak gains +4 to Constitution and becomes resistant to poison and ice-based attacks. In addition, the cloak adds Anti-Piercing resistance to all worn armor. It also makes you look like a dollar store Batman. Warning: if a Nightgaunt spies you wearing this, they probably won’t be too happy with you.
notes: Attached to Carl's leather coat. Occupies the neck slot.

canonical_name: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk
system_quote: Imbues wearer with +3 Strength and gives +3 to the Powerful Strike Skill…
notes: Worn on Carl's right index toe.

description: The Goblin Pass is a goblin skull tattoo that marks the bearer as a friend of the goblins. It is safe to assume that any crawler might receive this tattoo the first time they cause an explosion worthy of a Goblin Box.
system_quote: Now you’ll never get a good job!…
notes: Carl's left inner forearm.

description: The Desperado Pass is a tattoo that grants crawlers access to the Desperado Club, and may be received in an Asshole's Box and/or after a crawler earns their first Player-Killer Skull. The tattoo burns as it is applied to the crawler's neck (or, if a cat, above the right shoulder blade), and looks like a dagger dripping blood.
system_quote: Now you’re running with the type of kids who sit in the back of the bus…
notes: Carl's neck. Grants club access.

description: The Standard Healing Potion is red and contained in a corked glass bottle approximately 1/3 the size of a coke bottle. When consumed (rather than administered directly from inventory), it tastes like kiwi juice. It heals 50% + of a crawlers' health, but it has no effect on pets. The Standard Healing Potion is sorted under the "Potions" and "Healing" inventory submenus, and can stack up to 999 per slot.
system_quote: Increases your health by at least 50%…

description: Regular Mana Potions instantly and completely refill a character's Mana Points. These are commonly found in Loot Boxes on the first six floors of the Dungeon. : See Also: Good Mana Potion
An Iron Skin Potion (or Potion of Iron Skin) is a single-use consumable potion that increases a crawler's "physical armor" by 100% for 5 minutes.

A Skill Potion is a special potion that, when consumed, adds a single level to a skill specified in the item's description. Typically received in Loot Boxes, Skill Potions may be the only way to unlock certain Crawler Menu options such as sorting inventory by value.
system_quote: Drinking this adds a single level to the Determine Value skill…

description: Goblin Dynamite is an extremely volatile explosive created by Goblins. The red stick is wet and sticky, and the long wick hisses and pops like a sparkler when lit. The wick must be physically lit using a lighter or mechanism.
system_quote: The System AI whispers the description in its game show voice: Goblin Dynamite…

description: Category:Needs photo Goblin Smoke Bombs are apple-sized spherical bombs with wicks. After the wick is lit and the fire ignites the bomb, they emit a cloud of stinking, multi-color, opaque smoke that covers a 10 meter radius for three minutes (180 seconds) before dispersing.
system_quote: Most crawlers can only view cursory information about Goblin Smoke Bombs and other explosives…

description: Crawler Biscuits are food items that may be received in Bronze and Silver Adventurer Boxes.

Going through Third Floor Class race selection won't undo the changes from the Enhanced Pet Biscuit, but if the pet has been reclassified as a Crawler after using the biscuit, they can choose to change their race.
system_quote: So, it looks like a regular pet biscuit…

description: Experience Cookies look like chocolate chip cookie and taste stale but grant +10 experience (shared among party members) when consumed. A member of your party would get 0.2 of that experience. The experience notification appears above the crawler's head with an audible ping. These cookies may be found in limited-service Safe Rooms on the First Floor, where crawlers are limited to one per day.

A permacube generates heat when combined with combustible material such as coal. It has an extremely long lifespan and goes dormant when it runs out of coal, but does not turn off. It reactivates a few minutes after the material is shoveled in. In the Dungeon, Goblins use permacubes instead of Lesser Demons to power steam engines. : See Also: Goblin Copper Chopper

The Talisman of the Slate Butterfly is a small silver butterfly charm on a small silver ring, so it can be attached to collars or other jewelry. It jingles when it moves. See also: Stuffed Slate Butterfly Figure (Book 5)
system_quote: Talisman of the Slate Butterfly Those who remember and commemorate the sad tale of the Slate Butterfly are given a boon by the fairies of the…

description: Category:Needs photo Silver Ring is simple rings that, when equipped on a crawler's finger, boost a specific stat by a set value. They can be found in Silver Loot Boxes.

notes: Carl's own coat. The right sleeve is dissolved by a slime on the first floor.
Ill-fitting. What Carl was wearing when the Transformation hit.

canonical_name: Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph
description: The Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph is a black, zippered folder containing (12) metal pedicure tools. If the crawler makes a show of using some of the tools for ~15 minutes, multiple daily buffs will activate, and their feet will glitter.
system_quote: This kit contains 12 essential items for proper foot care…
notes: Carl begins using it on the second floor.

description: Carl's Jug O'Boom is crafted by emptying a clay Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine jug to about 3/4 full, adding a few ounces of Goblin Oil, and corking the bottle with a Torch. The crawler only has to look at the Torch, select "Activate" in their Heads-Up Display (HUD), and throw the bottle.
system_quote: Carl’s Jug O’ Boom Type: Incendiary Tossable Effect: When lit and tossed, results in a small explosion, followed by burning splash damage over a wide area…

description: Goblin Oil is a liquid combustible that can be mixed with other flammable substances to create highly effective incendiary weapons.
Mana Toast is a burned triangle of toast that restores mana.

A Boss Box is a specialized loot container that the Dungeon AI awards to the specific Crawler (or crawlers) responsible for killing a Boss. The box's tier corresponds to the boss's rank, ranging from Bronze for the weakest bosses up through Celestial for the strongest.

Goblin Boxes are a type of Loot Box awarded for using explosives, and generally contain more explosives. Carl received these on the first and second floors, and received similar loot in unspecified boxes on the Third Floor. The boxes appear to be haphazardly assembled with bits of metal, colored by tier, and have a goblin skull etched onto the lid.

Only a sponsor can send one, and the sponsor chooses the item personally. Because the contents come from outworld commerce rather than the dungeon's own loot tables, a box can deliver gear that is otherwise impossible to find inside, such as a pulse rifle or automated power armor.
A Magic Item Box is a type of Loot Box that appears to be awarded to crawlers who practice magic on the First Floor.
Mechanic's Boxes are Loot Boxes awarded for building contraptions inside the Dungeon. They typically contain crafting tools.
The Crowd Control Box is a Loot Box distributed for dispatching multiple mobs in a single attack.

Goblins are small, reckless, and mechanically gifted humanoids. They build complex steam-powered machines—using coal and water stored in a permacube instead of a lesser demon—including the Goblin Murder Dozer and Goblin Copper Chopper. Their society is structured around clan loyalty.
system_quote: What Goblins lack in physical strength they make up in pure spunk.

description: Slimes are toxic, arm-less mobs found on at least the First Floor and Seventh Floor of the Dungeon.
Rat-kin are bipedal, furry, rat-like creatures that stand around 5 ft (1.5 meters) tall. They appear to wear clothing.

Approximately 7 ft tall, Bugaboos look both "terrifying and cartoonish." They take the general shape of a bear with no neck, enormous owl-like eyes, "comically skinny legs," and long but "absurdly thin" arms. They are covered in obsidian-colored hair.
system_quote: You know that creepy, unkempt guy who lives on the corner?…

description: The Hoarder appears to be a 15' (4.5m) tall "enormously" obese human woman, approximately 35 years old, with matted black hair and open sores and scabs across her skin. She has only one tooth. She wears a filthy ripped t-shirt, no bra, and tight blue sweatpants with PINK on the leg.
system_quote: Trapped in her pile of rubbish, abandoned by society, the war inside her head has seeped out of her mind and infected both her body and…

description: Tusklings are pink-scorned orcs with wide warthog-like heads that sit too close to their shoulders and wide torsos about 1.5 times larger than a human's, but are comically stubby from the waist down; they stand roughly 4' 6" tall. Their faces are marked by black eyes and four crossed tusks: two long, curved tusks at the front, and a second pair further back. Some female Tusklings choose to pierce their tusks.

Troglodytes are muscular, humanoid mobs dressed in loincloths. Their head and torsos resemble Komodo dragons, but their scaly legs are long and bent, almost kangaroo-like. Their attacks may inflict a devastatingly painful Poison Debuff.
Chilly Goats are a mob found on the First Floor. They are white, horned goats with mouths full of fangs.

With giant yellow buckteeth and tan fur, Bad Llamas are approximately the size of a horse. A pouch in their throats allows them to spit red, baseball-sized gobs of scorching lava-spit from their mouths. It glows red when they prepare to spit; if the pouch is ruptured during this stage, it will burn the llama's throat and kill it. The lava spit smells of sulfur and cools from crimson to red.
system_quote: It’s a llama, but it’s bad…

description: Blender Fiends are an unknown mob type that initially populated the First Floor, but were relocated to a lower level some 62 hours after the Dungeon opened due to concerns that they may wipe out the crawlers.
Category:Needs photo Scat Thugs are level 3 First Floor mobs. They are bipedal racoon-headed monsters that stand approximately 2 ft tall, are roughly as strong as Goblins, and are armed with spears.

Kobolds are a Second Floor mob that resemble chihuahuas in size and appearance, but stand upright and walk on their hind legs. They wear metal caps with a spike, and chainmail armor that appears to have been made from beer tabs.
Brain Boilers look like a cross between a squid and an umbrella. They have a psionic attack that can be countered with high charisma. The Fear Spell is ineffective on them.
Small and troll-like with humanoid bodies and oversized heads, Clurichaun are marked by curly black hair, hooked noses, small feet, and very few teeth. They make a puglike gurgling noise when attack.
system_quote: If you hear banjo music, run…

description: Danger Dingoes are roughly the size of mastiffs (which typically stand 2' 6"+ tall and weigh 120-230 lbs), with absurdly long and sharp fangs that make them look "almost prehistoric." The fur on their faces looks like heavy metal corpse paint. When killed, they drop "Poor Dingo Pelts" and/or a few gold coins.
system_quote: The AI approximated a terrible Australian accent…

description: Category: needs photo are a mob found on the Second Floor and Fifth Floor.
system_quote: From the description of Ralph: Part earth rodent, part the embodiment of death, Frenzied Gerbils are regular mobs one might encounter on the fifth or seventh…

description: Mind Horrors are jellyfish-like floating brains with dangling tentacles. They are physically weak and move slowly, and their bodies have the "consistency of a jam-filled kickball"; sometimes they bounce when they hit the ground, sometimes they splatter. They have a psionic attack that does not seem to affect crawlers with high Intelligence, but causes a nearly debilitating health-sapping headache in other creatures.

Rage Elementals are creatures of intangible smoke and physical claws, capable of shredding a body into ribbons and raking up dungeon stone as they run. They are almost entirely non-corporeal: arrows shatter against the smoke without generating a health bar at all, and a Magic Missile raises only a flicker of one before the creature heals itself. That self-healing slows noticeably against burning damage.
system_quote: Rage Elemental – Level 93 The first recorded summoning of a Rage Elemental, blah, blah, blah…

description: Each Faction has an adjutant, who in turn has open communications with other teams' adjutants. Their participation is generally symbolic; they are typically flashy, famous characters like Odette who are there to give a running commentary to viewers during their daily, on-air recaps.

system_quote: The mysterious Agent Provocateur prides himself in being invisible…

description: Alpha Male Carl is a masculine caricature of Carl. He has gelled-back hair that Donut says is better than Carl's, and a prominent bulge in his star-patterned boxers. His War Gauntlet is bone-white rather than black. His patch jacket has two buttons: "#1 Son" and "Brother of the Century." He speaks in Carl's Father's voice.

system_quote: This is a regular arrow, but the tip is dipped in a poison that will inflict you with Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea…
This is a non-corporeal spirit. Also known as the Lord of Smallpox, Asojano is one of the most respected and feared of the Orishas, a former…

description: Babababoons are roughly human-sized and have simian bodies, complete with bright red asses. Their fleshy, "disconcertingly-human" faces have too-small features. They wear the sort of hoodlum outfits you'd expect to find in a Florida drunk tank: backwards baseball caps, top hats, ripped t-shirts featuring Nick Cage's face or rude statements, etc.

system_quote: Bang Bro Cost: 5 Mana Target: Temporarily Enchant Equipped Item Duration: 5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell…
Important inventions and discoveries of the 1900’s that changed the world…

description: Spell can be negated by a high enough Mind Balance Skill.

Big Boy Blues glowing, blue jellyfish, about 15' (4.572m) in diameter, with long tentacles. They drift aimlessly in water, bouncing off of each other, but will wrap their tentacles around crawlers who get too close.
